claims.claim: BNM onboarded both Maybank and CIMB to test tokenised deposits for payments.
claims.reason: S1 says BNM's DAIH onboarded tokenised deposits for payments by Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) and by CIMB Group Holdings Bhd.

claims.claim: The overlap between members is only a routine one (the tokenised-deposit testing).
claims.reason: S2 names a second overlap that is adverse: an analyst says CIMB and Maybank (along with AMMB) 'look more exposed' to mark-to-market fair-value losses as MGS yields rise. That is more than a routine overlap.

claims.claim: No shared adverse issue is evident.
claims.reason: S2 contradicts this. It names CIMB and Maybank as more exposed to Q3 fair-value losses from rising bond yields, and describes sector-wide NIM pressure from higher wholesale funding costs and deposit competition.
Neither source mentions Bangkok Bank, so nothing contradicts this.
